OTHER MORE ISOLATED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE OVER WESTERN PORTIONS OF THE PLAINS STATES...FROM THE DAKOTAS SOUTH TO THE TEXAS PANHANDLE.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: THE UPPER FLOW PATTERN ACROSS THE U.S. IS FORECAST TO TREND GRADUALLY TOWARD A QUASI-ZONAL REGIME...AS NUMEROUS SHORT-WAVE DISTURBANCES SHIFT EWD ACROSS THE COUNTRY SUPPRESSING THE SRN U.S. RIDGE. AT THE SURFACE...A BAROCLINIC ZONE IS FORECAST TO EVENTUALLY BECOME ESTABLISHED IN A ROUGHLY W-E FASHION FROM THE KS/OK VICINITY TO THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION...AS A WEAK SURFACE LOW TRACKS EWD ACROSS THE OH VALLEY WITH TIME. THIS BOUNDARY -- AND THE UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME N OF THE FRONT ACROSS THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS VICINITY -- WILL FOCUS THE MAIN AREAS OF CONVECTIVE ACTIVITY THIS PERIOD.

sections.title: THE OH/TN VALLEY VICINITY
sections.text: A RATHER DIFFICULT FORECAST WITH RESPECT TO CONVECTIVE EVOLUTION ACROSS THE OH VALLEY REGION IS EVIDENT ATTM...AS A VERY LARGE COMPLEX OF STORMS IS CURRENTLY MOVING SEWD ACROSS THE MID AND LOWER MO/MID MS VALLEY REGION. THIS COMPLEX OF STORMS -- IN VARIOUS STAGES OF DECAY WITHIN THE VARIOUS MODEL SOLUTIONS -- WILL LIKELY RESIDE OVER THE LOWER OH/MID MS VALLEY REGION EARLY IN THE PERIOD...WITH ANY ONGOING PRECIPITATION AND THE REMNANT CLOUD SHIELD LIKELY TO AFFECT THE DESTABILIZATION POTENTIAL OF THE DOWNSTREAM AIRMASS ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK. WITH THAT SAID...MODELS GENERALLY AGREE THAT AN AREA SE OF THE MAIN CONVECTIVE CONTAMINATION -- LIKELY CENTERED ON THE KY VICINITY -- SHOULD DESTABILIZE SUFFICIENTLY SUCH THAT NEW STORM DEVELOPMENT WILL OCCUR NEAR A CONVECTIVELY REINFORCED FRONTAL SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED/WEAK SURFACE LOW CROSSING THE OH VALLEY REGION. WITH MODERATELY STRONG/WEAKLY VEERING FLOW WITH HEIGHT TO RESIDE ACROSS THE AREA...STORMS SHOULD BECOME SEVERE -- WITH LIKELIHOOD FOR GRADUAL UPSCALE GROWTH FROM CELLULAR TO SMALL-SCALE LINEAR MODE. RISK FOR HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS CAN BE EXPECTED ALONG WITH A TORNADO OR TWO...WITH COVERAGE AND INTENSITY OF THE THREAT MODULATED TO S

sections.title: THE WRN DAKOTAS SWD TO THE TX PANHANDLE
sections.text: ELY LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE FLOW IS FORECAST TO EVOLVE ACROSS THE WRN HALF OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND VICINITY...IN A POST-FRONTAL FLOW REGIME N OF A W-E FRONT EXPECTED TO LIE FROM THE TX/OK PANHANDLE VICINITY ENEWD INTO THE MIDWEST BY LATE AFTERNOON. WITH THE UPSLOPE FLOW OCCURRING WITHIN A DIURNALLY DESTABILIZING ENVIRONMENT...EXPECT ISOLATED STORMS TO DEVELOP ACROSS THE CENTRAL AND NRN HIGH PLAINS AREA. IN ADDITION TO AMPLE CAPE...MODERATE WLY FLOW ALOFT ATOP THE LOW-LEVEL ELYS WILL RESULT IN SHEAR SUFFICIENT FOR ORGANIZED/ROTATING STORMS. THUS...LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGEST STORMS ACROSS THIS REGION. DURING THE EVENING/OVERNIGHT...STORM COVERAGE MAY INCREASE OVER SRN PORTIONS OF THE RISK AREA -- I.E. THE WRN KS/NWRN OK VICINITY -- AS A NOCTURNAL LOW-LEVEL JET INTENSIFIES. ALONG WITH THE RISK FOR ISOLATED HAIL/WIND SPREADING INTO THIS AREA...AN ISOLATED TORNADO WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE AS LOW-LEVEL SHEAR INCREASES. ..GOSS/MOSIER.. 06/04/2014

outlooks.summary: STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ACROSS THE OHIO/TENNESSEE VALLEY TODAY WITH A THREAT FOR MAINLY DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL...ALTHOUGH AN ISOLATED TORNADO MAY BE POSSIBLE. OTHER MORE ISOLATED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS MUCH OF THE NORTHERN AND CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AN INCREASINGLY ZONAL/PROGRESSIVE LONGWAVE PATTERN ACCOMPANIED BY A MODERATE BELT OF WESTERLIES WILL EXIST OVER THE NORTHERN TWO-THIRDS OF THE CONUS TO THE NORTH OF A SUBTROPICAL RIDGE CENTERED OVER NORTHERN MEXICO/SOUTHERN PLAINS. A FRONTAL BOUNDARY...REGIONALLY MODULATED BY EARLY DAY CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS AND OUTFLOW ACROSS THE MIDWEST...WILL GENERALLY MOVE SLOWLY SOUTH-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE SOUTH-CENTRAL PLAINS AND OH VALLEY/CENTRAL APPALACHIANS AND MID-ATLANTIC STATES THROUGH TONIGHT.

sections.title: OH/TN RIVER VALLEYS TO CENTRAL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: A RELATIVELY COMPLEX/MODEST CONFIDENCE SCENARIO EXISTS REGARDING SOME OF THE PARTICULAR DETAILS OF TODAYS SEVERE RISK. THIS IS LARGELY ATTRIBUTABLE TO A DECAYING MCS ONGOING EARLY THIS MORNING ACROSS THE MIDDLE MS RIVER AND OH VALLEYS. ASSOCIATED OUTFLOW/DENSER CLOUD COVER WILL HELP TO EFFECTIVELY DEFINE A ROUGHLY WEST-EAST FRONTAL BOUNDARY ACROSS THE REGION. SOUTH OF THIS CONVECTIVELY REINFORCED FRONT/MCS...THE BOUNDARY LAYER WILL BECOME MODERATELY UNSTABLE BY AFTERNOON VIA INSOLATION AND CONTINUED INFLUX OF LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE FROM THE WEST-SOUTHWEST. ESPECIALLY ON THE SOUTHERN FRINGES OF THE REMNANT EARLY DAY MCS...THIS SHOULD RESULT IN UPWARDS OF 2500-3000 J/KG OF MLCAPE ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE LOWER OH VALLEY AND THE MAJORITY OF THE TN VALLEY. THIS WILL GENERALLY BE IN THE PRESENCE OF 40+ KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR AS LOWER TO MIDDLE TROPOSPHERIC WINDS GRADUALLY VEER WITH HEIGHT. AS STORMS GRADUALLY INTENSIFY THROUGH THE AFTERNOON ON THE FRINGE OF THE DAY CONVECTION...SOME INITIAL SOUTHEASTWARD-MOVING SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF SEVERE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE ALONG WITH AN ISOLATED TORNADO RISK. HOWEVER...A RIBBON OF MODERATELY STRONG WEST-NORTHWESTERLY WIND ALOFT WILL MORE SO CONTRIBUTE TO THE

sections.title: MT/WY/CO TO THE HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: TO THE NORTH OF QUASI-STATIONARY SURFACE LOW ACROSS THE SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS AND A WSW-ENE ORIENTED FRONTAL BOUNDARY...LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE TRAJECTORIES WILL STEADILY INCREASE BY LATE AFTERNOON/EVENING WITH ASSOCIATED LOW-LEVEL MOISTENING ACROSS THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS. AT LEAST ISOLATED STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS SHOULD DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF EASTERN CO AND PERHAPS IMMEDIATELY NEAR/NORTHEAST OF THE SURFACE LOW/FRONTAL BOUNDARY BY LATE AFTERNOON/EVENING. LARGE HAIL WOULD BE THE PRIMARY CONCERN...BUT AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT MAY ALSO MATERIALIZE BY EARLY/MID-EVENING AS LOW-LEVEL SHEAR/MOISTURE INCREASE. STORMS MAY ORGANIZE AND SPREAD SOUTHEASTWARD TONIGHT ACROSS WESTERN/SOUTHERN KS AND NORTH/NORTHWEST OK WITH AID OF NOCTURNALLY STRENGTHENING LOW-LEVEL JET. FARTHER NORTH...AHEAD OF A SHORTWAVE TROUGH CROSSING THE NORTHERN ROCKIES/NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS...OTHER SEVERE TSTMS WILL BE POSSIBLE INITIALLY ACROSS PORTIONS OF SOUTHERN/EASTERN MT AND WY THIS AFTERNOON...PRIOR TO DEVELOPING INTO OTHER PARTS OF THE NORTH-CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS BY EVENING. 30-40 KT MID-LEVEL WESTERLIES AND MODEST BUOYANCY WILL ALLOW FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF SEVERE HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. outlooks.summary: STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ACROSS THE OHIO AND TENNESSEE VALLEYS TODAY THROUGH TONIGHT WITH A THREAT FOR MAINLY DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL...ALTHOUGH AN ISOLATED TORNADO CANNOT BE RULED OUT. OTHER ISOLATED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS MUCH OF THE NORTHERN AND CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MODEST MID-LEVEL ZONAL FLOW OF 35-60KT EXISTS FROM THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST ACROSS THE GREAT PLAINS TO THE OH VALLEY AND CNTRL APPALACHIANS TODAY...NORTH OF AN ELONGATED SUBTROPICAL RIDGE FROM NRN MEXICO/SRN PLAINS TO THE DEEP SOUTH. PRIMARY SYNOPTIC FRONT WAS SITUATED FROM DELMARVA WWD TO KS AND HAS A NUMBER OF PERTURBATIONS/WAVES ALONG IT...THE MOST PRONOUNCED OF WHICH IS A 1004MB LOW CENTERED NEAR IL/IND BORDER...SUPPORTED BY A CONVECTIVELY-REINFORCED MID-LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND 50-60KT SPEED MAX. THE FRONTAL LOW/WAVE WILL DEVELOP EAST TO OH/WV THROUGH TONIGHT AS THE TRAILING FRONT SINKS GRADUALLY SWD ACROSS THE OH RIVER. FARTHER WEST...THE FRONT WILL MAKE SLOWER SWD PROGRESS...BECOMING ESSENTIALLY QUASI-STATIONARY FROM SRN MO INTO SRN KS BY EARLY THURSDAY. FARTHER WEST..FROM THE SRN/CNTRL HIGH PLAINS NORTH TO THE CANADIAN BORDER...THE QUASI-STATIONARY SYNOPTIC BOUNDARY EXTENDS FROM THE NRN TX PANHANDLE NWD ALONG AND EAST OF THE FRONT RANGE. RELATIVELY STRONGER 12H 500MB HEIGHT FALLS ARE FORECAST ACROSS THE NRN PORTION OF THIS BOUNDARY...WITH GENERALLY WEAKER LARGE SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WITH SWD EXTENT.

sections.title: OH/TN RIVER VALLEYS TO CENTRAL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: FORECAST STORM EVOLUTION ACROSS THESE AREAS IS COMPLICATED BY REMNANTS OF OVERNIGHT AND CONTINUING EARLY-DAY CONVECTION AND MCS OUTFLOW WELL SOUTH OF SYNOPTIC FRONT. STRONGER LARGE SCALE ASCENT WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH UPPER SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND SFC FRONTAL WAVE MOVING FROM IND INTO OH THROUGH LATE AFTERNOON. THIS SUPPORT MAY BE CONTRIBUTING TO PERSISTING CONVECTION ALONG AND NORTH OF A WARM FRONTAL SEGMENT NEAR THE OH RIVER AT THIS TIME /REF MCD# 813/. SOME MOISTENING AND WARMING OF THE AIRMASS AHEAD OF THIS ACTIVITY...FROM WV INTO WRN PA MAY SUPPORT MODEST DESTABILIZATION. HOWEVER...GENERALLY WEAKER MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES MAY LIMIT MORE ROBUST UPDRAFTS FOR THE TIME BEING. WHILE MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES STEEPEN AND MOISTURE INCREASES WITH WWD EXTENT...FROM SRN OH WWD TO CONFLUENCE OF MS/OH RIVERS...LARGE SCALE ASCENT IN THE FORM OF MID-LEVEL HIGH FALLS WILL WEAKEN COINCIDENT WITH STRONG DESTABILIZATION. NONETHELESS...CONVECTIVE DEBRIS WAS ALREADY DIMINISHING ACROSS MUCH OF THE REGION ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE FRONTAL ZONE...FROM ERN MO ACROSS SRN IL AND WRN IND. EXPECT MLCAPE...WEAKENING INHIBITION...AND LOW LEVEL MASS CONVERGENCE NEAR THE FRONT TO AID RENEWED VIGOROUS TSTM DEVELOPMENT AL

sections.title: NRN/CNTRL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: AHEAD OF THE AFOREMENTIONED SHORTWAVE TROUGH/HEIGHT FALLS CROSSING THE NRN ROCKIES/NRN HIGH PLAINS...TSTMS SHOULD INCREASE AMIDST MODEST DESTABILIZATION BY LATE AFTERNOON. EXPECT ACTIVITY TO SPREAD EAST FROM SRN/ERN MT AND WY INTO ADJACENT AREAS OF THE NCNTRL HIGH PLAINS BY EVENING. 30-40 KT MID-LEVEL WLY FLOW AND MODEST BUOYANCY WILL ALLOW FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF SEVERE HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO. A FEW SOUTHEASTWARD-MOVING CLUSTERS MAY ULTIMATELY EVOLVE BY EARLY EVENING WITH A LOCALIZED WIND DAMAGE RISK SPREADING ACROSS PARTS OF THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS.

sections.title: CNTRL/SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: ACROSS THE SRN HIGH PLAINS...LOW-LEVEL UPSLOPE TRAJECTORIES WILL STEADILY INCREASE IN THE WAKE OF RECENT FRONTAL SURGE INTO THESE AREAS. WHILE LARGE SCALE SUPPORT FOR ASCENT WILL REMAIN SUBTLE...OROGRAPHIC AND DIABATIC EFFECTS SHOULD CONTRIBUTE TO AT LEAST ISOLATED STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS OVER ERN CO AND PERHAPS IMMEDIATELY NEAR/NORTHEAST OF WEAK SFC LOW/FRONTAL BOUNDARY. LARGE HAIL WOULD BE THE PRIMARY CONCERN...BUT AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT MAY ALSO MATERIALIZE BY EARLY/MID-EVENING AS LOW-LEVEL SHEAR/MOISTURE INCREASE. STORMS MAY ORGANIZE AND SPREAD EWD/SEWD INTO THE NIGHT...FOCUSED ALONG THE STALLED FRONT AND SUSTAINED BY STRENGTHENING NOCTURNAL LOW-LEVEL JET ACROSS WRN/SRN KS...AND PERHAPS NRN OK. ..CARBIN/SCHNEIDER.. 06/04/2014

outlooks.summary: STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL CONTINUE ACROSS THE OHIO AND TENNESSEE VALLEYS THROUGH PARTS OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS TO THE HIGH PLAINS THROUGH TONIGHT WITH A THREAT FOR MAINLY DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL. AN ISOLATED TORNADO CANNOT BE RULED OUT.

sections.title: SRN-SERN KS/NRN-NERN OK/SWRN MO/NWRN AR
sections.text: A SLIGHT RISK HAS BEEN EXPANDED TO INCLUDE THE REST OF SERN KS...NRN TO NERN OK...SWRN MO AND NWRN AR. SURFACE FRONT HAS MOVED SWD INTO SOUTH CENTRAL MO AND SERN KS...AND THEN EXTENDED SWWD INTO THE NRN TX PANHANDLE. STRONG SURFACE HEATING IN THE WARM SECTOR WITH MODIFICATION OF THE 18Z LAMONT OK SOUNDING PER A TEMPERATURE IN THE LOWER 90S AND DEWPOINTS INTO THE LOWER 70S HAS REDUCED THE INHIBITION OBSERVED EARLIER ACROSS THIS AREA. VISIBLE IMAGERY INDICATED DEEPENING CU INVOF THE SURFACE WIND SHIFT. GIVEN THE VERY STRONG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE 3000-4000 J PER KG/ AND THE PRESENCE OF STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR /UP TO 50 KT/...ORGANIZED STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS CAN BE EXPECTED WITHIN THIS CORRIDOR FROM SWRN MO INTO SERN KS. PORTIONS OF NRN-NERN OK AND NWRN AR WILL HAVE A THREAT FOR STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS AS ACTIVITY DEVELOPS SWD FROM SERN KS AND SWRN MO. MEANWHILE...POTENTIAL EXISTS FOR A SEVERE WEATHER THREAT TO AFFECT SRN-SERN KS AND ADJACENT NRN-NERN OK LATE TONIGHT AS FORECAST IN THE 1630Z OUTLOOK. STORMS MAY ORGANIZE AND SPREAD EWD/SEWD INTO THE NIGHT FROM THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...FOCUSED ALONG THE STALLED FRONT AND SUSTAINED BY STRENGTHENING NOCTURNAL LOW-LEVEL JET ACROSS WRN/S

sections.title: OH/TN VALLEYS
sections.text: EARLY-MID AFTERNOON SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWED AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE CONTINUED TO MOVE EWD THROUGH THE LOWER OH VALLEY...AND AT 19Z WAS LOCATED IN EAST CENTRAL INDIANA. A WARM FRONT EXTENDING ESEWD FROM THIS LOW HAD MOVED INTO SWRN OH TO WV...WHILE A TRAILING COLD FRONT HAS AND WILL CONTINUE TO ADVANCE SWD...WITH THE 19Z POSITION OF THIS BOUNDARY EXTENDING WSWWD FROM SRN IND/IL TO SOUTH OF STL IN MO. ENVIRONMENT ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR HAS BECOME MODERATELY-STRONGLY UNSTABLE THIS AFTERNOON GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF RICH MOISTURE /PW VALUES EXCEEDING 1.6 INCH AND SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S/ COMBINED WITH STRONG SURFACE HEATING AND ERN EXTENT OF STEEP LAPSE RATES. GIVEN THESE FACTORS AND SEVERAL HIGH RESOLUTION CONVECTIVE ALLOWING MODELS SUGGESTING ONE OR MORE FORWARD PROPAGATING MCS STRUCTURES MOVING SEWD ACROSS WRN-CENTRAL KY INTO MUCH OF TN...THE 30 PERCENT SEVERE WIND PROBABILITY HAS BEEN EXPANDED SOME...WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR STRONG-SIGNIFICANT WINDS SPREADING ACROSS THIS REGION INTO THE EVENING. TORNADO PROBABILITY HAS BEEN EXPANDED ACROSS THE OH VALLEY INTO SERN MO GIVEN GOOD HODOGRAPH CURVATURE WITH VERTICALLY VEERING WIND PROFILES.

sections.title: NRN AND CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: SMALL ADJUSTMENT TO THE SLIGHT RISK AND ATTENDANT SEVERE PROBABILITIES HAS BEEN MADE ACROSS SERN WY TO ACCOUNT FOR HAIL/WIND THREATS INTO THIS AREA. ..PETERS.. 06/04/2014 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT WED JUN 04 2014/

outlooks.summary: ISOLATED TO SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS WILL PERSIST ACROSS PARTS OF THE GREAT PLAINS TO THE SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS. AN ENHANCED RISK FOR A SWATH OF INTENSE DAMAGING WINDS EXISTS ACROSS PARTS OF KANSAS INTO NORTHEAST OKLAHOMA OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: GREAT PLAINS
sections.text: CONCERN IS INCREASING OVER THE POTENTIAL OF AN OVERNIGHT DERECHO EMANATING OUT OF ONGOING SCATTERED DISCRETE CONVECTION IN NERN CO. LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE RETURN WILL STRENGTHEN ON E TO SELY FLOW N OF THE QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT DRAPED FROM THE TX PANHANDLE TO FAR SERN KS AND SRN MO. THIS APPEARS TO BE IN RESPONSE TO A SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS WITH A SRN SPEED MAX TRACKING FROM THE SRN ROCKIES TO KS. A PLUME OF RICH BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE CHARACTERIZED BY LOWER 70S SURFACE DEW POINTS NEAR THE OZARK PLATEAU SHOULD BE ADVECTED INTO CNTRL KS. THIS WILL YIELD STRONG POTENTIAL BUOYANCY AMIDST VERY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. BUT WITH INCREASING MLCIN THIS EVENING...GREATER TO THE NW OF THE MOISTURE PLUME...UNCERTAINTY DOES EXIST IN THE SUSTENANCE/UPSCALE GROWTH OF THE ONGOING CONVECTION. THIS SEEMS TO BE REFLECTED WITH OSCILLATING SIMULATIONS IN RECENT HRRR RUNS. STILL...THE POTENTIAL DOES EXIST FOR UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A LONG-LIVED BOWING MCS /AS SIMULATED BY 12Z NSSL-WRF/ CAPABLE OF PRODUCING INTENSE SWATHS OF SEVERE WIND GUSTS GIVEN THE HIGH-END CAPE/SHEAR ENVIRONMENT. HAVE INCREASED SEVERE PROBABILITIES TO ACCOUNT FOR THIS POSSIBILITY.

sections.title: MID-SOUTH TO SRN APPALACHIANS
sections.text: SCATTERED TO NUMEROUS STORMS SHOULD GRADUALLY DIMINISH IN INTENSITY DURING THE LATE EVENING AND OVERNIGHT FROM EAST TO WEST AS NOCTURNAL COOLING ENSUES AND MID-LEVEL W/NWLYS SUBSIDE AS THE GREAT LAKES SHORTWAVE TROUGH SHIFTS EWD. THE GREATEST CLUSTERING OF STORMS INTO PARTS OF THE TN VALLEY SHOULD HAVE AN ENHANCED RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS THIS EVENING AS THE COLD POOL DEVELOPS SEWD. ..GRAMS.. 06/05/2014

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE RISK FOR LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL PERSIST ACROSS REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF THE WATCH INTO MID MORNING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONSIDERABLE WEAKENING OF A NE-SW-ORIENTED CONVECTIVE LINE SEGMENT HAS BEEN OBSERVED OVER THE PAST HOUR WITH INCREASING AMOUNTS OF STRATIFORM PRECIPITATION DEVELOPING DOWNSTREAM FROM THE PRIMARY CONVECTIVE BAND. WITHIN THIS BROADER REGIME...A LONGER-LIVED BOOKEND VORTEX OF CYCLONIC CHARACTER WILL PROGRESS EWD ACROSS THE MS RIVER /S OF STL/ WHERE THE HIGHEST PROBABILITY FOR DAMAGING WINDS WILL EXIST. ELSEWHERE ACROSS THE WATCH...GUSTY WINDS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE...BUT GIVEN THE WEAKENING TRENDS IN THE ONGOING STORMS...ORGANIZED SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL APPEARS TO BE DIMINISHING. ..MEAD.. 06/04/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WHILE NOT YET CERTAIN...DUE TO A SOMEWHAT MARGINAL ENVIRONMENT FOR SEVERE STORMS...IT IS POSSIBLE THAT CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT MAY EVENTUALLY INCREASE AND ORGANIZE SUFFICIENTLY TO REQUIRE A WATCH WITHIN THE NEXT FEW HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: PERSISTENT THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT...WITH FLUCTUATIONS IN INTENSITY...HAS BEEN DEVELOPING EASTWARD...ROUGHLY ALONG A LOW-LEVEL FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS PARTS OF NORTH CENTRAL KENTUCKY AND ADJACENT SOUTHERN OHIO. THIS HAS BEEN AIDED BY MOMENTUM ASSOCIATED WITH 30-40 KT WESTERLY MID-LEVEL FLOW...TO THE SOUTH OF A REMNANT CONVECTIVELY GENERATED CYCLONIC VORTEX MIGRATING THROUGH THE OHIO VALLEY. LOW-LEVEL FLOW AND SHEAR ARE GENERALLY WEAK AHEAD OF THIS ACTIVITY INTO THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS...BUT INSOLATION AND MOISTENING BENEATH MODESTLY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES ADVECTING TOWARD THE REGION FROM THE WEST WILL CONTINUE TO CONTRIBUTE TO DESTABILIZATION THIS AFTERNOON. AS INHIBITION GRADUALLY WEAKENS FOR BOUNDARY-LAYER BASED PARCELS CHARACTERIZED BY CAPE IN EXCESS OF 1000 J/KG...FURTHER CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT AND INTENSIFICATION IS PROBABLE ACROSS NORTHEAST KENTUCKY INTO CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN WEST VIRGINIA. GIVEN THE ENVIRONMENT...IT MAY NOT BE OUT OF THE QUESTION THAT A SUFFICIENTLY STRONG COLD POOL COULD EVENTUALLY FORM TO SUPPORT AN INCREASING RISK FOR STRONG SURFACE GUSTS WITH ACTIVITY AS IT SPREADS ACROSS CHARLESTON AND ADJACENT AREAS OF WEST VIRGINIA DURING THE 18-20Z TIME FRAME. WHILE PEAK GUSTS SEEM LIKELY TO REMAIN MOSTLY BELOW SEVERE CRITERIA...THEY COULD NEVERTHELESS STILL BE STRONG ENOUGH TO DOWN TREES/BRANCHES AND POWER LINES. AN ISOLATED TORNADO MAY NOT BE OUT OF THE QUESTION...PARTICULARLY WITH EARLY ACTIVITY NEAR THE FRONT...BUT THIS THREAT...IN GENERAL...SEEMS FAIRLY LOW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ONE OR MORE SEVERE WEATHER WATCHES PROBABLY WILL BE NEEDED ACROSS THE REGION THIS AFTERNOON...PERHAPS WITHIN THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO. SOME UNCERTAINTY EXISTS CONCERNING TIMING OF THE MORE SUBSTANTIVE INCREASE IN SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL. THIS SEEMS MOST LIKELY CLOSER TO THE 21-22Z TIME FRAME...BUT COULD OCCUR EARLIER.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TIMING OF SIGNIFICANT INCREASE IN CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ACROSS THE MIDDLE MISSISSIPPI INTO LOWER OHIO VALLEY REMAINS A BIT UNCLEAR. IN THE WAKE OF A COUPLE OF CONVECTIVELY GENERATED OR ENHANCED PERTURBATIONS...LATEST OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS STILL SUGGESTS INHIBITION FOR MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER PARCELS AHEAD OF A SOUTHEASTWARD ADVANCING FRONT...FROM PARTS OF SOUTHEAST MISSOURI AND SOUTHERN ILLINOIS INTO CENTRAL KENTUCKY...IS CONSIDERABLE. HOWEVER...AT LEAST SOME INCREASE IN CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ALREADY APPEARS EVIDENT ALONG THE SOUTHWARD ADVANCING EFFECTIVE COLD FRONT. INTO AND THROUGH THE 18-21Z TIME FRAME...FURTHER INSOLATION... BENEATH A CONTINUING INFLUX OF VERY WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR FROM THE PLAINS...LIKELY WILL CONTRIBUTE TO LARGE BOUNDARY LAYER CAPE IN THE PRESENCE OF STEEPENING MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. BENEATH 40-50 KT WEST NORTHWESTERLY 500 MB FLOW ON THE NORTHEASTERN PERIPHERY OF SUBTROPICAL RIDGING...WHICH IS EXPECTED TO BEGIN ERODING WITH AT LEAST WEAK MID-LEVEL HEIGHT FALLS LATER THIS AFTERNOON...THE ENVIRONMENT WILL BECOME CONDUCIVE TO DISCRETE SUPERCELL STORMS INITIALLY. UPSCALE CONVECTIVE GROWTH TO ONE OR MORE ORGANIZED AND CONSOLIDATING STORM CLUSTERS PROBABLY WILL BE FAIRLY RAPID...HOWEVER...WITH LARGE HAIL AND POTENTIALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREATS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONVECTIVE POTENTIAL ACROSS THE REGION THROUGH 18-21Z REMAINS A BIT UNCLEAR...BUT TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR THE POSSIBILITY OF AN INCREASING SEVERE WEATHER THREAT THAT COULD REQUIRE A WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ONGOING CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ACROSS AND SOUTHEAST OF THE WEST PLAINS MO AREA APPEARS MOSTLY ELEVATED IN NATURE...ROOTED WITHIN A ZONE OF ENHANCED LOWER TO MID TROPOSPHERIC WARM ADVECTION...ON THE NOSE OF VERY WARM...AND MORE STRONGLY CAPPING...ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR EMERGING FROM THE PLAINS. THE PERSISTENCE OF THIS FORCING REMAINS UNCLEAR...BUT WITHIN STRONGLY SHEARED WEST NORTHWESTERLY DEEP LAYER MEAN FLOW...ACTIVITY IS TENDING TO SPREAD TOWARD AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY AT LEAST SOMEWHAT PROGRESSIVELY WEAKER MID-LEVEL INHIBITION. AND IT DOES NOT APPEAR ENTIRELY OUT OF THE QUESTION THAT ACTIVITY COULD EVENTUALLY BECOME ROOTED IN THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER ACROSS LOWER PORTIONS OF THE MIDDLE MISSISSIPPI VALLEY. IF THIS OCCURS...CAPE FOR THE BOUNDARY LAYER PARCELS ACROSS THIS REGION IS BECOMING LARGE...AND SUPPORTIVE OF RAPID CONVECTIVE INTENSIFICATION. SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT AND UPSCALE GROWTH INTO AN ORGANIZATION CONVECTIVE CLUSTER WOULD THEN BE POSSIBLE...WITH INCREASING POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE HAIL/WIND GUSTS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR A POTENTIAL WW OVER THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS AS THUNDERSTORMS MOVE EASTWARD OFF HIGHER TERRAIN INTO AN ENVIRONMENT SUPPORTIVE OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WITH A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MID LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER WRN MT AND ERN ID HAS CONTRIBUTED TO EARLY DEVELOPMENT OF DEEP CONVECTION OVER SOUTH CENTRAL MT SWWRD INTO WY. A CHANNEL OF STRONGER MID LEVEL WINDS EXTENDS FROM NEAR THE TROUGH AXIS EWD OVER THE THREAT AREA...WITH RIW VWP 6KM WINDS OF 40KTS AT 1800UTC. EXISTING STORMS WILL PROGRESS EWD INTO AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY MLCAPE OF 1000-1500 J/KG AND 0-6KM SHEAR OF 35-45KT IN 1800 UTC SPC MESOANALYSIS FIELDS...WHICH WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELL STORMS WITH LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. HAIL SIZE GUIDANCE BASED ON SHORT TERM RAP POINT FORECAST SOUNDINGS INDICATE POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL FROM 1 TO 2 INCHES IN DIAMETER. HIGH PLAINS LOW RH SUB-CLOUD LAYER WILL ALSO SUPPORT DAMAGING WIND THREAT. THE TORNADO THREAT IS RELATIVELY LOW...WITH WEAK 0-1KM SHEAR AND HIGH LCLS...BUT AN ISOLATED TORNADO CAN NOT BE RULED OUT WITH STRONGER SUPERCELL STORMS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT APPEARS UNDERWAY...BUT MORE RAPID INTENSIFICATION STILL SEEMS AT LEAST A COUPLE OF HOURS AWAY. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR AN INCREASING SEVERE WEATHER THREAT THAT COULD REQUIRE A WATCH TOWARD 22-23Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SOME INCREASE IN CONVECTION IS NOW UNDERWAY ACROSS THE MISSOURI OZARKS. THIS IS OCCURRING IN ADVANCE OF A SOUTHWARD ADVANCING COLD FRONT...LIKELY IN RESPONSE TO CONTINUING BROAD LOW-LEVEL WARM ADVECTION. RATHER WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR STILL APPEARS TO BE ACTING TO SUPPRESS CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT...BUT WITHIN A RELATIVE WEAKNESS IN INHIBITION /REFLECTED IN 700 MB THERMAL FIELDS/...IT SEEMS PROBABLE THAT FURTHER BOUNDARY LAYER HEATING AND MIXING WILL EVENTUALLY CONTRIBUTE TO STORM INITIATION TOWARD THE 22-00Z TIME FRAME. IF/WHEN THIS OCCURS...AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND LARGE CAPE WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF RAPID INTENSIFICATION. IN THE PRESENCE OF STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR BENEATH 40-50 KT WEST NORTHWESTERLY 500 MB FLOW...SUPERCELLS ARE POSSIBLE INITIALLY...BEFORE CONVECTION ATTEMPTS TO CONSOLIDATE AND GROW UPSCALE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SUPERCELLS WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING A TORNADO DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS FROM FAR ERN KY INTO SRN OH AND WRN WV.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR SHOWS SEVERAL SUPERCELLS MOVING EWD ACROSS ERN KY...FAR SRN OH AND INTO WV AHEAD OF A SURFACE LOW. SWLY LOW-LEVEL FLOW IS HELPING TO MAINTAIN INSTABILITY ALONG A DIFFUSE WARM FRONT WHERE LOW-LEVEL SHEAR IS ALSO BEING MAXIMIZED WITH AROUND 200-300 M2/S2 EFFECTIVE SRH. LATEST KRLX RADAR SHOWS MULTIPLE COUPLETS ONGOING...SUGGESTING AT A MINIMUM STRONG WINDS DESPITE WEAK HAIL CORES. ..JEWELL.. 06/04/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE THUNDERSTORM THREAT IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE INTO THE EVENING...WITH A PRIMARY THREAT OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND. WW ISSUANCE MAY BE NECESSARY IN THE NEXT 1-2 HRS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING ACROSS ERN WY/WRN SD...WITH OTHER STORMS NOTED ALONG THE FRONT RANGE IN COLORADO. WHILE THE STRONGEST ACTIVITY HAS THUS FAR REMAINED NORTH AND WEST OF THE NEB PANHANDLE...STRONG TSTMS OVER ERN WY WILL MOVE INTO THE NWRN NEB PANHANDLE SHORTLY...WHILE ADDITIONAL STORMS MAY DEVELOP TO THE SOUTH...WITH DEVELOPING CU NOTED NEAR BFF. AN UPPER TROUGH MOVING INTO WRN WY WILL SUPPORT CONTINUING CONVECTION INTO THE EVENING. RELATIVELY MOIST SELY FLOW BENEATH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT MODERATE INSTABILITY...WHILE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR OF 40-50 KTS WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR SUPERCELL STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL...WITH SOME POSSIBLE UPSCALE GROWTH THIS EVENING INTO BOWING SEGMENTS CAPABLE OF LOCALLY ENHANCED DAMAGING WIND. WW ISSUANCE MAY BE REQUIRED SOON IN ORDER TO COVER THIS THREAT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED SEVERE TSTMS WILL BE POSSIBLE FOR A FEW HOURS THIS EVENING...WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL THE PRIMARY THREAT. RELATIVELY LIMITED MAGNITUDE AND DURATION OF THREAT MAKES WW ISSUANCE UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SEVERAL STRONG TO SEVERE TSTMS HAVE DEVELOPED ACROSS NRN ND...WITH SEVERE HAIL RECENTLY NOTED NEAR MINOT. ADDITIONAL ATTEMPTS AT INITIATION ARE OCCURRING FURTHER SOUTH INTO CNTRL ND. THIS ACTIVITY IS DEVELOPING IN ADVANCE OF A COMPACT UPPER TROUGH CURRENTLY MOVING ACROSS SRN SASKATCHEWAN. MODEST MLCAPE OF 500-1500 J/KG AND EFFECTIVE SHEAR OF 25-35 KTS WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED MULTICELLS AND PERHAPS AN ISOLATED SUPERCELL STRUCTURE...WITH A PRIMARY THREAT OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL. WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED AT THIS TIME...THOUGH TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS WILL CONTINUE SWD ACROSS KY AND INTO TN THIS EVENING. THE TORNADO THREAT IS GREATEST IN KY...WITH DAMAGING WINDS EVENTUALLY SPREADING SWD INTO TN. A NEW WATCH WILL BE NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A BROKEN LINE OF SEVERE STORMS CONTINUES TO SHIFT SEWD ACROSS THE LOWER OH VALLEY INTO WRN KY BENEATH A STRONG MIDLEVEL JET MAX AND IN A STRONGLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS. WIND PROFILES CONTINUE TO BE FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS AS WELL AS BOWS WITH NWLY FLOW ALOFT AND NEAR THE INSTABILITY AXIS. A NEW WATCH WILL BE REQUIRED PRIOR TO EXPIRATION TIME...AND ALSO EXTENDING INTO TN.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO INCREASE IN INTENSITY WITH LARGE HAIL AND LOCALLY STRONG WINDS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CELLS ARE INCREASING OVER SWRN MO ON THE WRN FRINGE OF THE MORE CONFLUENT LOW-LEVEL FLOW AND WARM ADVECTION. THE 00Z SGF SOUNDING SHOWED VERY STRONG INSTABILITY AND AMPLE SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND STRONG DOWNBURSTS. GIVEN CURRENT LIGHTNING TRENDS...IT APPEARS THIS WEAK FORCING WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR AT LEAST ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS THIS EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE TSTM THREAT CONTINUES IN AND NEAR WW 221. DOWNSTREAM WATCH ISSUANCE ACROSS CNTRL SD/N-CNTRL NEB IS UNLIKELY GIVEN WEAKENING TREND IN THIS AREA. UPSCALE GROWTH REMAINS POSSIBLE ACROSS NERN CO WHERE A SUBSTANTIAL WIND-PRODUCING MCS MAY EVOLVE LATER THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONVECTION HAS EVOLVED INTO A PAIR OF BOWING SEGMENTS ACROSS WRN SD INTO THE NRN NEB PANHANDLE THIS EVENING. INCREASING CINH AHEAD OF THESE SYSTEMS HAS LED TO A RECENT DECREASE IN INTENSITY AND THE LONGEVITY OF THESE SYSTEMS IS EXPECTED TO BE RELATIVELY LIMITED...MAKING THE NEED FOR EVENTUAL WATCH ISSUANCE UNLIKELY AT THIS TIME. TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED FOR THE NEXT 1-2 HRS DOWNSTREAM OF THE NRN PART OF WATCH 221. FURTHER SOUTH INTO NERN CO...DISCRETE STORMS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WIND...AND PERHAPS AN ISOLATED TORNADO CONTINUE...WITH A RECENT UPTICK IN INTENSITY NOTED NW OF LIC. WHILE ANY DISCRETE CELLS MAY BEGIN TO STRUGGLE WITH INCREASING SBCINH IN THE SHORT TERM...ANYTHING THAT REMAINS OF ONGOING CONVECTION LATER THIS EVENING...COMBINED WITH POTENTIAL ELEVATED STORM INITIATION AS WAA INCREASES IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE LOW-LEVEL JET...MAY EVENTUALLY CONGEAL INTO A SEWD-MOVING MCS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING WIND INTO WRN KS. MUCH OF THE NEB PANHANDLE HAS REMAINED MOSTLY FREE OF CONVECTION...BUT STORMS HAVE BEGUN TO INCREASE IN THE LAST HOUR W OF AIA/BFF. A WINDOW OF OPPORTUNITY REMAINS FOR INTENSE STORMS FOR 1-2 HOURS THIS EVENING IN THIS AREA BEFORE SBCINH WILL BEGIN SUPPRESSING SURFACE-BASED CONVECTION. ..DEAN.. 06/05/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A FEW SEVERE STORMS REMAIN POSSIBLE THIS EVENING MAINLY ACROSS ERN KY AND TN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: INITIAL ACTIVITY HAS STABILIZED MUCH OF THE ERN PARTS OF THE WATCH...BUT OTHER STORMS CONTINUE TO EVOLVE ACROSS ERN KY AND TN...FUELED BY WLY LOW-LEVEL THETA-E ADVECTION. THEREFORE...WHILE ACTIVITY APPEARS NON-SEVERE ACROSS THE WW AT THIS TIME...ADDITIONAL STORMS WILL POSSIBLY MOVE IN FROM THE W LATER THIS EVENING. ..JEWELL.. 06/05/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WATCH ISSUANCE IS POSSIBLE SOON DOWNSTREAM OF INTENSE SUPERCELL COMPLEX. A NEAR-TERM TORNADO/HAIL THREAT EXISTS...WITH POTENTIAL FOR EVENTUAL UPSCALE GROWTH AND AN INCREASING DAMAGING WIND THREAT OVERNIGHT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: INTENSE SUPERCELL RECENTLY PASSED THROUGH LIMON CO WITH LARGE HAIL AND A REPORTED TORNADO. WITH THIS SUPERCELL COMPLEX APPROACHING THE EDGE OF WW 221 IN ABOUT AN HOUR...DOWNSTREAM WATCH ISSUANCE IS BEING CONSIDERED. WHILE SBCINH IS INCREASING OVER THE AREA...MODERATE TO STRONG BUOYANCY AND VERY FAVORABLE WIND PROFILES /AS NOTED IN THE PUX VWP/ WILL HELP SUSTAIN THE SUPERCELL COMPLEX IN THE SHORT TERM AS IT MOVES DOWN THE INSTABILITY GRADIENT. VERY LARGE HAIL AND ISOLATED TORNADOES WILL CONTINUE TO BE POSSIBLE. LATER THIS EVENING...ADDITIONAL CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT AIDED BY AN INCREASING LLJ MAY RESULT IN UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A SEWD MOVING MCS THAT WOULD AFFECT FAR ERN CO INTO WRN KS...WITH AN INCREASING THREAT OF DAMAGING WIND. ..DEAN.. 06/05/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS...HAIL AND AN ISOLATED TORNADO PERSISTS ACROSS MUCH OF TN WITH THE GREATEST THREAT FROM WRN INTO MIDDLE TN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LINE OF STORMS CONTINUES TO EVOLVE ESEWD NOW EXTENDING FROM NWRN INTO NRN MIDDLE TN. LOW-LEVEL WINDS CONTINUE TO BE FAVORABLY ORIENTED TO PROVIDE STORM RELATIVE INFLOW AS THE CELLS PROPAGATE SEWD. CELLS OVER NW INTO MIDDLE TN WILL CONTINUE TO HAVE ACCESS TO THE MOST UNSTABLE AIR VIA WLY LOW-LEVEL FLOW. NW-SE ORIENTED DEEP LAYER SHEAR IMPLIES STORMS COULD MAKE IT INTO FAR NRN AL AND GA LATER TONIGHT...BUT INSTABILITY MAY NOT BE GREAT ENOUGH FOR AN ADDITIONAL WATCH AS STORMS LEAVE THE INSTABILITY AXIS. ..JEWELL.. 06/05/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A WATCH WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED WITHIN THE HOUR FOR ADDITIONAL PORTIONS OF WESTERN/CENTRAL KS. AN APPRECIABLY INCREASING RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS WILL LIKELY BE THE MOST PROMINENT CONCERN INTO PORTIONS OF WESTERN/CENTRAL KS...BUT SOME RISK FOR AN EMBEDDED TORNADO AND/OR EPISODIC LARGE HAIL MAY EXIST AS WELL.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: EARLIER SEMI-DISCRETE SUPERCELLS CONTINUE TO STEADILY GROW UPSCALE INTO A BROADER/INTENSE MCS WHILE STILL MAINTAINING SOME EMBEDDED SUPERCELL STRUCTURES ACROSS FAR EAST-CENTRAL CO JUST SOUTH OF I-70 AS OF 0620Z. TO THE IMMEDIATE NORTH OF A SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS SURFACE LOW/ANGLING FRONT BOUNDARY...STRENGTHENING SOUTH-SOUTHEASTERLY WINDS JUST ABOVE EASTERLY BOUNDARY LAYER WINDS WILL CONTINUE TO RESULT IN AMPLE WARM/MOIST ADVECTION NEAR/AHEAD OF THE EVOLVING MCS. THESE ADVECTIONS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH A RESERVOIR OF AMPLE MOISTURE/INSTABILITY ACROSS SOUTHERN KS/NORTHERN OK AS PER 00Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS FROM DODGE CITY AND LAMONT OK /2000-3500 J PER KG MLCAPE/. LATEST WSR-88D VWP DATA FROM DODGE CITY INDICATES THAT SOUTHEASTERLY WINDS AROUND 1-2 KM HAVE INCREASED TO AS MUCH AS 40 KT. ALL SAID...CONTINUED UPSCALE EXPANSION OF AN INCREASINGLY ORGANIZED/ACCELERATING QUASI-LINEAR MCS SEEMS LIKELY TO OCCUR THROUGH THE EARLY/MIDDLE PART OF THE OVERNIGHT ACROSS PORTIONS OF WESTERN/CENTRAL KS. AS THIS SYSTEM ORGANIZES/ACCELERATES EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD...POTENTIALLY WIDESPREAD/LOCALLY INTENSE DAMAGING WINDS ARE LIKELY TO BECOME AN INCREASING CONCERN.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND RISK MAY CONTINUE FROM SOUTHERN MIDDLE TN/PARTS OF SOUTHEAST TN SOUTHEASTWARD INTO NORTHERN PARTS OF AL/GA THROUGH THE MIDDLE PART OF THE OVERNIGHT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A RELATIVELY SMALL BUT WELL-ORGANIZED LINEAR CLUSTER WILL LIKELY CONTINUE TO MOVE SOUTHEASTWARD INTO PORTIONS OF NORTHERN AL/NORTH GA OVERNIGHT. ALTHOUGH INTENSITY SHOULD GRADUALLY WEAKEN...A SURFACE COLD POOL AND MCV INFLUENCES WITH A STRONG BELT OF MID-LEVEL WINDS /50+ KT ABOVE 4 KM AGL PER REGIONAL WSR-88D VWPS SUCH AS HPX AND OHX/ WILL LIKELY ALLOW ORGANIZED LINEAR STRUCTURES TO PERSIST SOUTHEASTWARD. AT LEAST LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS SHOULD REMAIN A CONCERN AS STORM CLUSTERS SPREAD SOUTHEASTWARD OVERNIGHT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE TSTM WATCH 224 CONTINUES PRINCIPALLY ACROSS SOUTHWEST MO THROUGH 10Z WITH A CONTINUED RISK FOR ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS. A SEVERE RISK COULD DEVELOP INTO PARTS OF FAR NORTH AR BUT AN ADDITIONAL SEVERE TSTM WATCH IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS INCLUDING A SLIGHTLY ELEVATED HP SUPERCELL AS OF 0730Z WILL LIKELY TO CONTINUE TO POSE A SEVERE HAIL AND PERHAPS AN ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND RISK OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. THIS ACTIVITY CONTINUES TO FOCUS NEAR/JUST NORTH OF A CONVECTIVELY REINFORCED BOUNDARY ACROSS FAR SOUTHERN MO IN ASSOCIATED WITH A WEAK WARM ADVECTION/ISENTROPIC LIFT REGIME. SIMILAR TO THE 00Z OBSERVED SOUNDING FROM SPRINGFIELD MO...THE AMBIENT AIR MASS REMAINS AT LEAST MODERATELY UNSTABLE WITH UPWARDS OF 2000+ J/KG MUCAPE IN THE PRESENCE OF AMPLE VERTICAL SHEAR...A SCENARIO FAVORABLE FOR HP-TYPE SUPERCELL STRUCTURES/WELL-ORGANIZED LINE SEGMENTS OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. WHILE ACTIVITY MAY DEVELOP INTO FAR NORTHERN AR OVERNIGHT...AN ADDITIONAL WATCH IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED OWING TO RELATIVELY MARGINAL/ISOLATED NATURE OF THE RISK. ..GUYER.. 06/05/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: INTENSE/POTENTIALLY WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WIND POTENTIAL IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE THROUGH 10Z-12Z ACROSS MUCH OF CENTRAL KS IN ASSOCIATION WITH AN EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD MOVING QUASI-LINEAR MCS/BOW ECHO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONSEQUENTIAL UPSCALE QUASI-LINEAR GROWTH CONTINUES TO OCCUR ACROSS WESTERN KS AS OF 0830Z VIA AN 80-MILE NORTH-SOUTH EXTENSIVE LINEAR MCS AND A PRECEDING WARM ADVECTION-TYPE CORRIDOR OF STRONG/LOCALLY SEVERE TSTMS. THE FORWARD MOTION OF THE MCS HAS NOW GENERALLY REACHED 40 KT...AND ADDITIONAL FORWARD PROPAGATION/ACCELERATION WILL OCCUR OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS AS STORMS MERGERS CONTINUE WITHIN AN INCREASINGLY MOIST ENVIRONMENT. A 50+ KT FORWARD MOTION SHOULD EVOLVE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS /POTENTIALLY BY 10Z-11Z/. AHEAD OF THE MCS...SURFACE PRESSURE FALLS CONTINUE TO OCCUR PRINCIPALLY ACROSS SOUTHWEST/SOUTH-CENTRAL KS WHERE 3+MB/2HR FALLS ARE NOTED IN CONJUNCTION WITH A SLIGHT INCREASE OF SURFACE DEWPOINTS /NEAR 70 F/. AN INCREASINGLY STRONG EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD LOW-LEVEL INFLUX OF WARM/UNSTABLE AIR NEAR/JUST ABOVE THE SURFACE WILL ALLOW THE MCS TO CONTINUE TO THRIVE WHILE OTHERWISE GROWING UPSCALE/FORWARD ACCELERATING. IN THE IMMEDIATE WAKE OF THE MCS...50-60 KT WESTERLY MID-LEVEL WINDS ARE NOW EVIDENT BETWEEN 4-6 KM AGL IN WSR-88D VWP DATA FROM GOODLAND/DODGE CITY KS...WHICH NOT ONLY SPEAKS TO THE STRENGTH OF THE AMBIENT MID-LEVEL FLOW /ALIGNED PERPENDICULAR TO THE MCS/ BUT ALSO EVOLVING MCV-TYPE ENHANCEMENTS. OVERALL...A NUMBER OF FACTORS SUGGEST THAT AN INCREASINGLY INTENSE MCS/BOW ECHO WILL CONTINUE TO ACCELERATE EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD THROUGH THE EARLY MORNING HOURS. IN SPITE OF NEAR-SURFACE INHIBITION...A POTENTIALLY WIDESPREAD WIND DAMAGE RISK APPEARS LIKELY INTO CENTRAL KS. ..GUYER.. 06/05/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A POTENTIALLY WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WIND THREAT...AND PRECEDING ISOLATED LARGE HAIL RISK...IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE ACROSS MUCH OF EASTERN KS THROUGH THE EARLY MORNING HOURS. A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH WILL BE NEEDED PRIOR TO 10Z/5AM CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SEVERE MCS/BOW ECHO IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE TO ACCELERATE GENERALLY EASTWARD TOWARD EASTERN KS THROUGH THE EARLY MORNING HOURS...WHILE AHEAD OF IT...ISOLATED INSTANCES OF LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY AMPLE ELEVATED INSTABILITY/SHEAR THROUGH THE CLOUD-BEARING LAYER. FOR ADDITIONAL SHORT-TERM METEOROLOGICAL DETAILS...REFERENCE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 830.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WIDESPREAD WIND DAMAGE REMAINS AN APPRECIABLE CONCERN ESPECIALLY FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTH-CENTRAL/EAST-CENTRAL AND SOUTHEAST KS EARLY THIS MORNING. THIS INCLUDES THE I-135 VICINITIES AND KANSAS TURNPIKE. ISOLATED BOUTS OF LARGE HAIL WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE AS WELL. IN ALL LIKELIHOOD...AN ADDITIONAL WATCH WILL BE NEEDED SOON FOR AREAS POTENTIALLY INCLUDING SOUTHWEST/WEST-CENTRAL MO AND NORTHEAST OK/NORTHWEST AR.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: IN SPITE OF SOME NEAR-SURFACE INHIBITION...CONCERN REMAINS HIGH FOR POTENTIALLY WIDESPREAD WIND DAMAGE EARLY THIS MORNING IN ASSOCIATION WITH A SIGNIFICANT MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM. EMBEDDED EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD FORWARD MOTIONS HAVE REACHED AS HIGH AS 60 KT...WITH A SIGNIFICANT /WESTERLY/ REAR INFLOW JET NOTED IN VOLUMETRIC RADAR DATA ACROSS CENTRAL KS IN THE IMMEDIATE WAKE OF THE MCS. THIS COMPLEX CONTINUES TO UNFOLD JUST NORTH OF A DEEPENING SURFACE LOW/NEARBY WNW-ESE FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS FAR SOUTHERN KS/NORTHERN OK...WITH A CONSEQUENTIAL SURFACE PRESSURE FALL/RISE COUPLET NOTED VIA A 2MB/2HR PRECEDING FALLS AND TRAILING SURFACE COLD POOL/MESO-HIGH. FAST-MOVING EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD BOWING BRUNT OF THE MCS ASIDE...AN ASYMMETRIC EVOLUTION APPEARS TO BE OCCURRING...AND AS SUCH...NORTH-SIDE EMBEDDED BOOKEND VORTICES COULD ALSO BE SOME CONCERN. WIND DAMAGE ASIDE...ISOLATED INSTANCES OF LARGE HAIL WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE WITH MCS-PRECEDING STORMS. ..GUYER.. 06/05/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
